fatal_errors: It places the relevant tribo-corrosion service conditions above 600 °C, whereas the target experiments were conducted in deionized water at 25–100 °C; approximately 1100 °C was only a brief thermal-shock conditioning step.
It replaces the specific as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA and its L12/B2 lamellar microstructure with a nominally homogeneous, homogenized AlCoCrFeNi alloy.
It implies continuous high-temperature oxide-scale protection and service stability that were not demonstrated by the target study.
explanation: The response recovers the broad conclusion that an Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-family HEA can outperform conventional alloys in combined wear and corrosion, and it proposes a generally falsifiable comparison using wear, friction, electrochemistry, microscopy, and phase analysis. However, it misses the defining material composition and eutectic L12/B2 lamellar state, the DS2205 comparator, and nearly all critical test conditions. Most importantly, it conflates rapid thermal-shock conditioning near 1100 °C with tribo-corrosion service above 600 °C, while the actual sliding tests occurred in immersed deionized water from 25 to 100 °C. Its generic self-healing oxide explanation only weakly overlaps with the observed competition among depassivation, repassivation, tribo-layer stability, abrasion, and third-body wear, and it omits the minimum degradation near 50 °C. Thus it is a coarse partial reconstruction rather than an exact account.
